characterList.description: A man with dark, medium-length hair, wearing a navy blue suit and a white shirt. He's the speaker and appears to be giving a press conference.
characterList.name: Justin Trudeau

content_metadata.description: Video of Justin Trudeau giving a press conference, focusing on transparency, youth employment, and international issues.

qAndA.answer: He mentions hospitality and travel expenses, particularly in regards to hospitality and travel.
qAndA.question: What specific types of expenses does Trudeau say the Liberal Party will proactively disclose online?

qAndA.answer: He talks about young people facing some of the worst summer job numbers ever recorded in Canada and the need for expanded opportunities in education, training, and the knowledge economy.
qAndA.question: What are some of the concerns facing young people that Trudeau mentions?

qAndA.answer: He says the point is to bring together Liberal members from across the country who have heard from Canadians concerned about their jobs, future, and pensions and to begin working together to develop solutions.
qAndA.question: What does Trudeau say is the point of the caucus meeting?

qAndA.answer: He states that the Liberal Party will be proactively disclosing their expenses online, following a similar model to the ministerial accountability measures introduced by former Prime Minister Paul Martin in 2004.
qAndA.question: What specific example of transparency and accountability does Trudeau announce in the video?

qAndA.answer: His formal attire, serious facial expression, and the setting of a press conference held at a golf course, which contrasts the usually relaxed atmosphere of golf.
qAndA.question: What visual cues reinforce the serious tone of Trudeau's message?

scenes.contextualRelevance: Trudeau emphasizes the need for a new approach to politics, highlighting transparency and accountability as key values. His focus on youth employment and economic opportunity suggests a desire to address the concerns of a generation facing significant challenges. His condemnation of the use of chemical weapons in Syria and his call for Canada's involvement underscores a commitment to global humanitarian efforts.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: We had an extraordinary,
successful meeting this morning.
Caucus is energized and excited,
having spent a summer talking with Canadians
in their constituencies and across the country
about the change that Canadians want to see
and from their government, from their politicians.
We had many discussions on a variety of subjects,
including obviously the struggles of the middle class
and the need for robust economic solutions
to the many challenges that we're facing.
We talked a lot about openness and transparency
and accountability to Canadians.
There was a lot of discussion about that
and consistent with that, we have decided
that even though Mr. Harper has decided to pro-Rogue
and keep away from Parliament for four extra weeks this fall,
the Liberal Party will be returning in the third week
of September as expected to get to work serving Canadians
through the work in Ottawa that they expect us to do.
We as a party had announced in the spring
that we will be proactively disclosing our expenses online,
particularly in regards to hospitality and travel expenses,
along the same model that ministers,
the ministerial accountability that is demanded
and has been demanded since 2004 since Paul Martin,
Liberal Prime Minister, brought in those measures.
So we will be following along the very similar lines
to the ministerial disclosure.
And we intend to start when we return to Ottawa in late September.
We are expecting that the example that the Liberal Party
is going to show in being open and honest
and disclosing our expenses
is going to mean that the other parties will choose to follow suit.
I think Canadians demand a level of transparency
from the governments and from the political parties
that the Liberal Party is happy to step up to
and happy to take the lead on.
I know that the other parties will not take long to realize
that they cannot operate in secrecy anymore from Canadians.
We've been talking an awful lot about the concerns
facing young people particularly,
young people who are facing some of the worst summer job numbers
that Canadians have ever recorded.
But it's not just young people who are lacking in opportunities.
It's parents who are finding a larger role in having to support
their children for longer.
Looking at education and training,
looking at how we're expanding opportunities in the knowledge economy,
looking at how we develop solutions across the board
is what the Liberal Party will be focused on over the coming years.
We have a policy platform to build for 2015
and we are serious about putting it together in consultation
with experts with academics and with ordinary Canadians.
The point of this caucus is to bring together the Liberal members
from across the country who have heard from Canadians
who are concerned about their jobs, about their future,
about their pensions and begin to work together
to develop the solutions that we're going to bring in as a government in 2015.
This is not something to take lightly.
It's not something to reel off on because people want answers.
People want answers, but people want to be part of generating those answers.
And that's where the Liberal Party is absolutely serious
about the kinds of meaningful consultation and working with Canadians
to build a platform that reflects both the priorities,
concerns and solutions that Canadians are generating across the country.
On youth, employment and internships throughout the summer,
we will continue to engage with Canadians in public forums.
We will have a platform in 2015, a robust and comprehensive.
We will have multiple discussions on economics,
on concerns that we have and solutions we're bringing forward
throughout the coming two years.
And it will be an ongoing concern that we address.
We are talking about it, we are working with it,
and we will continue to address these concerns openly with Canadians
and develop solutions.
There will be a various numbers of stakeholder meetings.
We will have round tables on issues that are important to Canadians.
We will be discussing solutions we have to bring forward.
We will be doing the kind of work that Parliamentary committees
and parliamentarians are expected to do in terms of both holding the government
to account for its erroneous decisions and its poor judgment,
but also proposing the kinds of solutions
and bringing together the kinds of stakeholders
who provide input and solutions.
The bringing Canadians on inside involves involving them in our discussions,
being open and consultative and iterative in our policy development,
which means we put out ideas, they generate feedback,
we continue to build with Canadians, the kinds of solutions,
and future that they expect.
My responsibility is to put forward a comprehensive robust platform in 2015
that is going to demonstrate to Canadians that the Liberal Party is serious
about working hard for them responding to their concerns.
And I'm not going to shortcut that process, which is a serious and responsible process
just because people want to know right now, and they're impatient to know in the right time.
We will be responsible about how we approach this and are not worried
about dominating the news of the day.
We want to provide good government to Canadians
because that's what they deserve.
Thank you.
I had a briefing yesterday afternoon from Minister Beard,
who shared with me the information on the conversations
that the government has been having with our allies in the U.S.
and in the UK and elsewhere.
We continue to be extremely concerned about what's happening in Syria,
the Syria people, up to 100,000 people
have been killed, 400,000 injured.
The use of chemical weapons is unacceptable and requires this significant response
from the international community.
And I am fully expecting that Canada will have a role to play in keeping
in helping civilians, helping the Syrian people move beyond these atrocities.
What exactly that role will be is something that we should be discussing
as Canadian parliamentarians, which is why I certainly like to see
parliament recalled so we can discuss this.
But it's not an issue upon which I'm going to play any partisan games
or advantage. Canadians, all Canadian parliamentarians are united
in our horror, what's going on in Syria, in our desire to help
humanitarian aid, greater help in terms of refugees.
These are things that Canada can do and the Canadians are united and wanting to do.
But certainly supporting the international community and its decisions to
intervene is going to be something that Canada will continue to pursue.
Are you following for Parliament to be your candidate?
Thank you.
All right. Thank you.
One with my side.
Of course.
He's going to be at an engineer.
Very pleased to meet you.
Good luck.
You're very well spoken.
Thank you.
Thank you.
For yourself, mate.
Thank you.
Hey.
So?
Yeah?
What's that?
How's it going?
It's a good thing.
It's a good thing.
It's a good thing.
It's a good thing.
It's a good thing.

youtube_description: Federal Liberal Leader Justin Trudeau and his caucas were at a golf resort in Brudenell, PEI for their summer  meetings.  He took some time to talk to the media about 4 themes he says his party is working on which includes; Transparency, Middle-class economic policies, Election preparations and Leadership.
youtube_title: August 28, 2013 Justin Trudeau Interview-Liberal Caucus Summer Meetings
